zh.title: 布魯塞爾航空擴增2026/27冬季北極航線 增闢挪威與芬蘭航點
zh.summary: 布魯塞爾航空宣布2026/27冬季開辦挪威埃文斯與芬蘭凱米、基蒂萊航線。
body: 布魯塞爾航空（Brussels Airlines）於2026年8月17日宣布，將在2026/27年冬季班表期間，大幅擴增前往歐洲遠北地區的網絡運能。這家比利時國家航空將開辦從其樞紐布魯塞爾扎夫特姆機場（BRU）出發、前往三個北極航點的定期航線，包含鄰近挪威北部羅弗敦群島的埃文斯（EVE）、位於波斯尼亞灣北端且靠近瑞典邊境的芬蘭凱米（KEM），以及作為芬蘭拉普蘭地區門戶之一的基蒂萊（KTT）。
根據布魯塞爾航空公布的航線時程，往返布魯塞爾與基蒂萊的航線將於2026年12月10日至2027年3月27日期間營運，每週提供三個班次；凱米航線則於2026年聖誕節（12月25日）至2027年3月10日營運，每週提供兩個班次。至於埃文斯航線，則僅於2027年2月與3月期間營運，每週提供一個班次。

布魯塞爾航空表示，新增北極航線主要是為了回應旅客對獨特冬季景致、未受破壞的自然環境以及觀賞極光等活動持續成長的需求。過去幾年間，多家歐洲航空公司相繼擴增前往北歐高緯度地區的服務，使該市場從傳統上以聖誕節前夕與聖誕主題為主的家庭旅遊，轉型為吸引更廣泛客群的特色旅遊。布魯塞爾航空隸屬於漢莎航空集團（Lufthansa Group），截至2026年3月，該集團旗下航空公司在冬季月份每週運營多達69班從中歐與西歐出發、前往北極圈附近航點的航班。
除了布魯塞爾航空的新開航線外，同集團的德國國家航空漢莎航空（Lufthansa）亦將開辦慕尼黑（MUC）至羅瓦涅米（RVN）的全新直飛服務，並將慕尼黑往返基蒂萊的航班增至每週兩班。此外，法蘭克福前往拉普蘭地區羅瓦涅米與庫薩莫（KAO）的航班頻率亦將提升，而挪威北部的特羅姆瑟（TOS）往返法蘭克福與慕尼黑的航線也將各增加兩個班次。

en.title: Bru (BRU)ssels Airlines Expands Arctic Network with New Services to Norway and Finland
en.summary: Brussels Airlines expands its 2026/27 winter network with new scheduled flights to Norway and Finland.
body: Brussels Airlines announced on August 17, 2026, that it will significantly increase capacity to Europe's far north during the 2026/27 winter season. The Belgian flag carrier is launching scheduled service between its base at Brussels-Zaventem Airport  and three Arctic destinations. These destinations comprise Eve (EVE)nes , near northern Norway's Lofoten archipelago, Kem (KEM)i  in Finland near the Swedish border at the northern end of the Gulf of Bothnia, and Kittilä (KTT), a gateway to Finnish Lapland.

The airline outlined specific seasonal flight schedules for the three new Nordic routes. The service connecting Brussels to Kittilä  is scheduled to run three times weekly between December 10, 2026, and March 27, 2027. The route to Kemi  will operate twice weekly from Christmas Day 2026 through March 10, 2027. Finally, flights to Evenes  will operate once per week specifically during February and March 2027.

According to Brussels Airlines, expanding into these northern destinations responds to rising passenger demand for unique winter landscapes, unspoilt nature, and Northern Lights viewing opportunities. Over recent years, multiple European airlines have expanded services to the Nordic region, shifting from seasonal, Santa Claus-focused family travel to a broader travel niche. Brussels Airlines operates as part of the Lufthansa Group, whose member airlines operated up to 69 weekly flights during winter months as of March 2026 between Western and Central Europe and destinations near the Arctic Circle.

Alongside Brussels Airlines, German flag carrier Lufthansa is launching a new nonstop service between Munich (MUC) and Rovaniemi (RVN), while adding a second weekly frequency between Munich and Kittilä . Frankfurt will see increased frequencies to both Rovaniemi and Kuusamo (KAO) in Lapland. Additionally, Tromso (TOS (TOS)) in northern Norway will receive two additional frequencies connecting to both Frankfurt and Munich.

zh.title: 樂天協助德國Helsing向日本陸上自衛隊推廣HX-2攻擊無人機
zh.summary: 樂天協助德國Helsing推廣無人機；日本陸自進行HX-2測試至9月底
body: 日本樂天集團已證實，正協助德國國防科技公司Helsing向日本陸上自衛隊推銷HX-2攻擊型無人機。樂天表示，日本陸上自衛隊目前正在對HX-2無人機進行實地測試，相關測試預計將持續進行至2026年9月底。
Helsing指出，該公司於2026年早些時候在當地經紀夥伴的協助下，已與日本當局達成初步協議。HX-2為一款重12公斤、射程達100公里的電動X翼巡飛彈，具備自主搜尋與攻擊目標的機載人工智慧系統。日本預計將在評估測試結果後決定是否引進該系統。
樂天執行長三木谷浩史的幕僚長向路透社表示，國防領域初創企業面臨複雜的採購體系與漫長的獲取週期等結構性障礙，樂天計畫利用其網絡協助此類公司對接日本政府的國防需求。

en.title: Rakuten Assists German Startup Helsing in Pitching HX-2 Drone to Japan Military
en.summary: Rakuten supports Helsing's HX-2 strike drone pitch to Japan as field trials run through September 2026.
body: Rakuten has confirmed it is assisting German defense tech company Helsing in pitching its HX-2 strike drone to the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force. Field evaluations of the drone by the Japanese military are currently underway and scheduled to continue through the end of September 2026.

Helsing stated that it reached an initial agreement with Japanese authorities earlier in 2026 through a local partner. The HX-2 is an electrically propelled x-wing loitering munition weighing 12 kilograms with a range of up to 100 kilometers. Japan is expected to decide on potential procurement after evaluating trial results.

Hideaki Mukai, chief of staff to Rakuten CEO Hiroshi Mikitani, told Reuters that defense startups face structural procurement barriers and lengthy acquisition cycles. Mukai noted that Rakuten intends to leverage its network to connect technology companies with Japanese defense requirements.
